relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a boy with a NOD2 variant: 'Genetic analysis at the age of four years revealed a de novo p. Arg334Trp variant in the NOD2 gene, which supported a diagnosis of EOS/BS'.
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; JSON assembled by a short Python script from hand-chosen values and spans, then every span checked verbatim against the paper. One in-scope person (label 'patient', single unnamed patient of a case report). The twin and the mother are mentioned only in passing (birth; mother noticed skin lesions) and are not described as affected or tested, so no rows. Inheritance left 'not reported' although the paper calls the variant 'de novo': no parental testing is described (rule 8 / D-24); parental_testing_statement therefore 'not reported'. Zygosity, variant type and pathogenicity not stated for this variant. The protein string is printed with a space ('p. Arg334Trp') and kept as printed; no cDNA or transcript printed. Age at last evaluation taken from the abstract ('9-year-old'); the most recent ophthalmological exam was at 8 years. Age at diagnosis is that of the genetic diagnosis ('at the age of four years'); the patient was earlier diagnosed with JIA at an unstated age after age 3. The ophthalmological examination at age 2 was reported normal as a whole; recorded as an excluded 'abnormal ophthalmological examination' row (excludes nothing more specific; uveitis developed later). Glaucoma is recorded from the Discussion ('secondary glaucoma'); the case text describes secondary angle closure. Vital status 'alive' inferred from current treatment statement. No contradictions found.
